claim: Binder migrates toward the coating surface during drying of graphite anodes (binder gradient through the coating); the consultant links substrate adhesion to local binder concentration at the collector.
quantity_bounded: Binder concentration profile through coating thickness
threshold_or_direction: direction: binder depleted at the collector side -> lower adhesion (FM01, FM09)
applies_if: Wet-processed graphite/binder/carbon-black coating; through-thickness axis and collector interface known.
cannot_cover: Our frames: no collector interface confirmed in frame, thickness axis unknown, binder lumped into class 0/1 (unobservable).
observed: Title, venue and consultant summary only; abstract not delivered by Crossref and full text not read in this PR.
inferred: FM01/FM09 are unobservable in our data; this claim only documents the mechanism.
source_locator: J. Power Sources 318:210-219 (2016); consultant handoff S01.

claim: For thicker aqueous graphite anodes, loss of adhesion becomes a more serious problem under certain drying conditions, and cracking occurs at a certain drying rate and with increasing electrode thickness; the cause is binder transported to the surface during drying.
quantity_bounded: Adhesion and crack occurrence vs drying rate and coating thickness
threshold_or_direction: direction: faster drying / thicker coating -> more adhesion loss and cracking (FM01, FM07, FM16); no numeric bound transferable
applies_if: Aqueous graphite/CB/CMC/SBR coatings; drying-stage cracks at coating scale.
cannot_cover: Crack identity in our sections (coating crack vs FIB curtaining A01 vs particle fissure); drying parameters of the supplied material are unknown.
observed: Abstract: 'loss of adhesion associated with certain drying conditions becomes a more serious problem; cracking occurs at a certain drying rate and with increasing electrode thickness'.
inferred: Supports FM07 as a plausible manufacturing mode worth a detector; does not say what a crack looks like in a FIB cross-section.

claim: Intensive dry mixing of anode materials fixes carbon black on the active-material surface, decreasing electrical conductivity while changing binder/carbon-black/active-material interactions and long-term cycling.
quantity_bounded: Carbon-black / binder network distribution vs conductivity
threshold_or_direction: direction only: redistribution of the conductive/binder network changes conductivity and cohesion (FM02, FM03)
applies_if: Graphite anode with carbon black and binder; mixing route known.
cannot_cover: Carbon black and binder are not resolved as classes in our segmentation (lumped into class 0/1); conductivity is not an image quantity.
observed: Abstract: 'decrease in electrical conductivity, due to the fixation of carbon black particles on the active materials' surface'; anode dry-mixing study.
inferred: FM02/FM03 remain unobservable or proxy-only here.

claim: The slurry mixing sequence changes graphite dispersion and the resistance of lithium-ion anodes at identical composition; the consultant reports higher resistivity for agglomerated electrodes.
threshold_or_direction: direction: poorer dispersion / persistent agglomerates -> higher resistance (FM08 -> FM03); no numeric bound
applies_if: Graphite anode slurries; dispersion measured by the study's own methods.
cannot_cover: Whether adjacent class-2 objects in a 2D section are a persistent agglomerate or touching particles; our F06 Clark-Evans R is acquisition-confounded (see FMC19).
observed: Title and venue; abstract not delivered by Crossref; the resistivity statement is the consultant's summary.
inferred: FM08 is proxy-only via F06/F05 and currently supports `investigate` at most.
source_locator: J. Colloid Interface Sci. 625:136-144 (2022); handoff S04.

claim: Artificially introduced particle contamination and line defects on anodes affected specific capacity over cycles and thermal behaviour of cylindrical cells, whereas point (pinhole) defects did not significantly affect cell behaviour.
quantity_bounded: Cell capacity and thermal response vs anode defect type
threshold_or_direction: direction: contamination and line defects harmful (FM04, FM06); pinholes not shown harmful (FM19)
applies_if: Plan-view inline inspection of coated anodes (optical camera, laser thermography); contamination introduced deliberately.
cannot_cover: Identification of bright BSE objects in our sections as contaminants (needs EDS); mm-scale line defects are outside a ~7000 px field.
observed: Abstract: 'point defects do not significantly affect cell behaviour. However, line defects and particle contamination on the anodes were observed to impact both the specific capacity over cycles and its thermal behaviour'.
inferred: Justifies routing FM04 candidates to `investigate` + EDS request; never `outside bounds` from BSE brightness alone.

claim: Inline optical line-scan inspection of electrodes uses a catalogue of typical coating defects (stripes, pinholes, wrinkles, imprints, edge defects) classified from surface brightness differences; causes and effects are proposed from literature and expert experience.
threshold_or_direction: none (taxonomy); causes/effects are expert judgement in the source
applies_if: Plan-view web inspection during coating; not anode- or graphite-specific.
cannot_cover: FIB cross-sections of a few hundred micrometres; cathode mud-crack mechanisms are not transferred.
observed: Abstract: 'the catalog of typical defects, and the image features used to classify them'; 'causes and effects ... on the basis of the literature and expert experience'.
inferred: FM06, FM12, FM17, FM19, FM20 are plan-view/roll-scale modes and are out of scope for our data.

claim: Poor electrode cut quality leads to performance degradation, separator protrusion and local electric stress concentration; laser-cut anode edges are classified into five geometric types from SEM images.
threshold_or_direction: direction: poor edge geometry harmful (FM05, FM18); no bound transferable
applies_if: A manufacturing cut edge is imaged; cutting route known.
cannot_cover: Our frames contain no confirmed manufacturing edge; the FIB-milled face is a preparation surface (A02), not a cut edge.
observed: Abstract: 'poor cut quality leads to performance degradation, separator protrusion, and local electric stress concentration'; 'Five types of classification ... presented and explained with SEM images'.
inferred: Grade B because the consequence statement is introductory context in a laser-process paper; FM05/FM18 are out of scope here.

claim: In a graphite anode design-of-experiments (active material 80-96 wt%, carbon black 1-10 wt%, CMC 1-3 wt%, SBR 1-7 wt%), viscosity-increasing components improve adhesion by improving dispersion and hindering binder migration; coating conductivity is sensitive to the collector-coating interface.
quantity_bounded: Formulation weight fractions vs slurry/coating properties
threshold_or_direction: direction only: formulation changes adhesion, dispersion and conductivity (FM10, FM02, FM11); the tested ranges are a research design space, not acceptance limits
applies_if: Aqueous graphite anode formulation; composition known.
cannot_cover: Conversion of class-2 area fraction to wt% (composition and class identities unconfirmed; Si vs SiOx indistinguishable).
observed: Abstract gives the DoE ranges quoted and 'Viscosity increasing components also improve adhesion, by improving dispersion and hindering binder migration'.
inferred: FM10 stays proxy-only via F02 and supports `investigate` only.

claim: Calendering parameters change the microstructure and density of graphite anodes, detectable by ultrasonic testing; the consultant reports thickness-dependent density and acoustic response.
quantity_bounded: Graphite anode density / microstructure vs calendering line load
threshold_or_direction: direction: more compaction -> higher density, lower porosity (FM13); 'greater compaction is not universally better or worse' (consultant)
applies_if: CMC/SBR graphite anodes with known calendering parameters.
cannot_cover: An absolute porosity bound for our class-0 fraction (0.10, below every published electrode porosity found in PR #5 L4, which PR #5 attributes to measurement definition).
observed: Title and venue; abstract not delivered by Crossref; density statement is the consultant's summary.
inferred: FM13 can use F01/F08/F09 as relative, batch-vs-reference proxies only.

claim: Electrode wettability responds non-monotonically to calendering in a graphite/CMC/SBR/carbon-black electrode (consultant read full text); pore geometry matters alongside total porosity.
threshold_or_direction: non-monotonic: no single direction; therefore 'direction only: departure from reference in either sense is a question, not a defect' (FM13, FM14)
applies_if: Graphite anodes compacted to different degrees; wetting measured directly.
cannot_cover: Wetting itself (not an SEM quantity); 3D pore connectivity and tortuosity (A06).
observed: Title and venue; abstract not delivered by Crossref; non-monotonic statement is the consultant's full-text reading.
inferred: Prevents any rule that treats lower or higher class-0 fraction as better; FM14 rules are two-sided and relative to Batch_3.

claim: Moisture sorption, uptake kinetics and moisture levels of cell components (including anodes) vary along the production process; moisture is a hidden quality variable without an SEM appearance signature.
threshold_or_direction: none transferable (FM15, FM16)
applies_if: Moisture measured by the study's methods (not imaging).
cannot_cover: Any SEM image in vacuum; moisture is unobservable in our data.
observed: Title and venue; abstract not delivered by Crossref; summary is the consultant's.
inferred: FM15/FM16 out of scope; listed under 'cannot decide'.

claim: With increasing silicon content in silicon-graphite anodes, elastic deformation (springback) of the coating rises, overall porosity is less affected than the pore size distribution, electrical conductivity decreases independent of coating density, and long-term electrochemical stability deteriorates with silicon content and coating density.
quantity_bounded: Springback, porosity, pore size distribution, conductivity vs Si mass fraction and line load
threshold_or_direction: direction: more Si -> more springback, lower conductivity, altered pore size distribution (FM21, FM22, FM10, FM14); conditional on class 2 = Si
applies_if: Class 2 is silicon-bearing (stated by Polaron, not image-verified; consultant: unconfirmed) and the material was calendered.
cannot_cover: Si vs SiOx; adhesion to the collector (no interface in frame); conductivity (not an image quantity).
observed: Abstract: 'with increasing silicon content, the elastic deformation of the electrode coating rises'; 'overall porosity ... less affected by silicon than the pore size distribution'; 'electrical conductivity decreases at higher silicon contents independent of coating density'.
inferred: Supports treating F08 (pore thickness distribution) rather than F01 alone as the FM14/FM21 proxy; still `investigate` only.

claim: FIB-SEM images of a Si/C-graphite anode show curtain artefacts, reduced by a Fourier-transform filter; shine-through artefacts were removed manually before global-threshold segmentation of active material and pores.
quantity_bounded: Curtaining and shine-through in FIB-SEM anode images
threshold_or_direction: none; artefact existence and mitigation (A01, A03, A04)
applies_if: FIB-SEM cross-sections of porous Si/C-graphite anodes.
cannot_cover: Our curtaining_score calibration; serial-section 3D (we have single sections).
observed: Abstract: 'Fourier transform-based filter that effectively reduces curtain artifacts'; 'requires user interactions such as ... removing shine-through artifacts manually'.
inferred: A01 and A03 are real in this material class; any crack or pore rule must exclude them first.

claim: Lift-out specimen preparation for Li-ion electrodes (including pristine graphite/Si-C) addresses redeposition and curtaining as preparation artefacts in correlative FIB-SIMS/SEM work (consultant summary).
threshold_or_direction: none (A02 exists; no covariate measures it in our pipeline)
applies_if: FIB-prepared electrode specimens.
cannot_cover: Identification of bright objects in our images (the study knew its composition).
observed: Title and venue; abstract not delivered by Crossref; redeposition statement is the consultant's.
inferred: A02 is a standing, unmeasured caveat; cannot be excluded as a confound, so no rule reaches `outside bounds` on grey-level evidence alone.
source_locator: ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16(42):57141-57150 (2024); handoff S15.

claim: The binarization procedure applied to X-ray tomographic data of lithium-ion electrodes affects the quantitative microstructural parameters extracted.
quantity_bounded: Microstructural descriptor uncertainty from segmentation choice
threshold_or_direction: none transferable; the paper's numbers are tomography-specific (A04)
applies_if: Any thresholded phase map (our class maps included, qualitatively).
cannot_cover: The magnitude of segmentation uncertainty in our SEM images (must be measured by our own two segmentation variants).
observed: Abstract: 'The procedure for binarization of X-ray tomographic data affects the quantitative analysis of microstructural parameters in lithium ion battery electrodes.'
inferred: Every F01-F11 rule must survive both segmentation variants before escalation.

claim: Geometric parameter estimation of battery electrode microstructure from 2D image sections is associated with ambiguity; spatially dependent parameters such as tortuosity and pore-phase connectivity need volume-based 3D characterization.
threshold_or_direction: none; limits what 2D sections can decide (A06, FM14)
applies_if: 2D sections of nonconvex, irregular, interconnected particles (our case).
cannot_cover: Tortuosity, connectivity, 3D agglomerate size (never claimed here).
observed: Abstract: 'geometric parameter estimation using 2-D image sections is bound to be associated with ambiguity'; 3D needed for 'tortuosity and pore-phase connectivity'.
inferred: Pore-architecture rules are restricted to 2D descriptors (F08, F09, F10) and stay relative to Batch_3.
source_locator: J. Microsc. 263(3):280-292 (2016); handoff S18; also taiwo2016 in PR #5.

claim: SEM magnification/length measurements require a calibrated standard with stated measurement uncertainty (NIST SRM work).
threshold_or_direction: none; nm statements only 'if 25 nm/px is true' (A05)
applies_if: Any conversion of px to nm.
cannot_cover: The actual calibration of the supplied instrument (res_tag only, not independently verified).
observed: Title, venue and year via Crossref; the handoff gave no DOI; DOI located by Crossref bibliographic search; text not read.
inferred: All nm columns stay labelled *_nm_if25; no rule uses nm thresholds.

claim: Backscattered-electron yield increases with mean atomic number, so BSE grey level ranks local composition by Z but does not identify it; elemental identification needs X-ray microanalysis (EDS).
quantity_bounded: BSE grey level vs mean atomic number
threshold_or_direction: direction: brighter BSE = higher mean Z candidate (FM04); identity requires EDS
applies_if: BSE imaging of a flat section (our BSE channel).
cannot_cover: Whether a bright object is a metallic contaminant, Si, SiOx, or redeposited material (A02); charging halos (edge_charging) can also brighten.
observed: Book title and publisher via Crossref; standard textbook content, specific passage not quoted here.
inferred: FM04 candidates from a per-object brightness/size outlier screen can only produce `investigate` + EDS request.
source_locator: Goldstein et al., Scanning Electron Microscopy and X-Ray Microanalysis, 4th ed., Springer (2018).

claim: F06 (class-2 Clark-Evans R, per image) differs between acquisition groups (image height x resolution tag, 13 groups) more than between batches: permutation Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0077 across acquisition groups vs p = 0.052 across batches; Spearman rho = 0.53 with BSE mean grey level.
threshold_or_direction: none; shows acquisition confounding of the FM08 proxy
applies_if: results/features/features_by_image.csv (PR #3) joined to results/artefacts_per_image.parquet (BSE) and results/audit/images.csv; 3000 label permutations, seed 0.
cannot_cover: Causal direction (acquisition vs material) - groups are partly nested in batches.
observed: Computed in this session on the PR #3 outputs; medians by batch 0.734 / 0.678 / 0.724 (Batch_1/2/3).
inferred: FM08 cannot escalate beyond `investigate` until F06 is residualised against acquisition covariates and re-tested at image level.

claim: F05 (class-2 count density per Mpx) also differs by acquisition group (permutation Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0007) but not by batch (p = 0.70); Spearman rho = 0.47 with BSE mean grey level.
threshold_or_direction: none; acquisition confounding of a second FM08 proxy
applies_if: Same computation as FMC19.
cannot_cover: Same as FMC19.
observed: Computed in this session on the PR #3 outputs.
inferred: F05 is a covariate-sensitive feature; not usable as an independent line of evidence for FM08.

claim: Consultant importance weights (5/4/3/2 and '4, conditional') are editorial ordinal estimates for research prioritisation: not occurrence probabilities, calibrated severities, risk-priority numbers or thresholds, with no specified mathematical aggregation.
threshold_or_direction: none; routing/priority hint only
applies_if: Prioritising which modes to screen or present first.
cannot_cover: Any score, multiplier or verdict.
observed: Handoff section 'Context and meaning of the weights'.

claim: Composition and Si/SiOx of the supplied electrodes remain unconfirmed (consultant), while Polaron states class 2 = silicon, class 1 = graphite, class 0 = void/pore ('stated by Polaron, not image-verified').
threshold_or_direction: none; both positions recorded, not resolved
